facts.label: Oferecer e recusar com educação
facts.sub: Use Would you like + some/a + coisa? ou Would you like to + verbo? para oferecer. Responda Yes, please ou No, thanks, I’m full.

facts.label: Você gostaria…?
facts.sub: Use Would you like + some/a + comida para oferecer: Would you like some more brisket? Would you like a glass of lemonade? É mais educado que Do you want…? Responda com Yes, please.

facts.label: Não, obrigado
facts.sub: Recuse com No, thank you ou No, thanks, e dê uma razão curta: I’m full. It’s delicious, but I’m full. Não precisa pedir desculpa. Um sorriso ajuda muito.

compare.us: Em inglês, use Would you like + some more + comida ou Would you like to + verbo. Para recusar, diga No, thank you, I’m full.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Would you like…? is a polite offer.
We answer an offer with “Yes, please” or “No, thanks”.
We say “Do you want some more?” only at formal dinners.
items.why: Do you want… is fine with friends; Would you like… is more polite.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Would you like…? is a polite offer. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We answer an offer with “Yes, please” or “No, thanks”. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “Do you want some more?” only at formal dinners. → Falso (Do you want… is fine with friends; Would you like… is more polite.)

pages.title: A dining room in Austin · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a warm Sunday evening in Austin. Earl and his friend Zoe sit in the dining room. The table is full of food and plates. A big plate of brisket sits in the middle. The sauce smells sweet and smoky. Earl is a generous host and loves to offer more.

“Zoe, would you like some more brisket? There’s plenty left.” says Earl. “It’s delicious, but no, thanks. I’m really full. Maybe later.” says Zoe. “Of course. Would you like a glass of lemonade, then?” says Earl.
